implementation.name: JTRIDERS
implementation.notes: Source availability (T5.4): open -- the HDL lives in the jotego/jtcores monorepo at cores/riders/, 24 source files. There is no open_source column in the delivered schema (data-model.md §1.9 deleted the proposed core table together with its flags); the presence of hdl_language_id, license_id and implementation_path rows is how that fact is stated here. license_id omitted: the repository LICENSE is the verbatim GPLv3 text but no any-later-version grant was found in https://github.com/jotego/jtcores/blob/master/cores/riders/doc/053936.v, so the version scope is not something this core's own files state. Machine mapping: 26 MRA files in jotego/jtbin's mra/ directory name <rbf>jtriders</rbf>; 4 setnames resolved exactly to a MAME 0.288 machine and 22 through MAME's own cloneof relation to the parent that survives extract/machine.json's parents-only filter, giving 4 distinct machine_id rows. hdl_language_id: 22 of 24 HDL files are verilog (2 systemverilog, 22 verilog), excluding the shared framework directory. accuracy_id omitted: jotego's README claims faithfulness in prose but states no timing-fidelity level this build could check against data/lookup/accuracy_level.json. Dependency deliberately not recorded: cores/riders/cfg/files.yaml has a rungun: entry, but the only file it pulls is jt053936.v -- jotego's model of the Konami 053936 PSAC2 rotation/zoom custom chip (its header reads Date: 12-7-2025), which lives in cores/rungun/hdl only because Run and Gun is the core it was first written for. No implementation_dependency row is written: the shared thing is a custom-chip module that has no implementation record of its own, not the JTRUNGUN core. cores/rungun/cfg/files.yaml pulls jt054321.v back out of cores/riders/hdl on exactly the same basis, so writing both edges would also close a dependency cycle.
